sectors.name: Restaurant (neighbourhood)
sectors.mix_note: visitor share 24%: the two restaurant types average to the DSEC tourism ratio 62.2% (2024)

sources.item: Subsidy 4% p.a., loan cap MOP 5m, up to 3 years, SME with at most 100 staff, MOP 10bn pool
sources.source: Macao News on the DSEDT scheme

sources.item: Scheme continued in the 2026 Policy Address (18 Nov 2025)
sources.source: HRO summary of the 2026 Policy Address

sources.basis: Latest bank notice found (ICBC Macau, effective 3 Nov 2025; HSBC had cut to 5.375% on 24 Sep 2025). AMCM composite funding cost barely moved in 2026 (1.16% to 1.15%, Q1 to Q2), so no sign of a further cut.
sources.source: ICBC (Macau) notice; AMCM composite interest rate Q2 2026

sources.basis: Only 45% of new SME credit is collateralised (AMCM, H1 2026), so most SME credit is unsecured and priced above prime. The subsidy pays the full 4% either way; the spread only changes the part firms pay, and the sensitivity table shows results barely move between +0 and +3pp.

sources.item: Loan size = 11 months of fixed costs (cap MOP 5m)
sources.basis: Scheme average loan MOP 2.26m (MOP 3.8bn over 1,682 approvals, to 21 Jan 2026) divided by the average establishment's monthly fixed cost MOP 206k (DSEC 2024 retail and restaurant surveys) = 11.0 months.
sources.source: DSEDT reply to the Legislative Assembly, Feb 2026

sources.item: Loans are interest-only credit lines, already drawn and spent
sources.basis: AMCM reports SME lending as credit limits with an 84.1% utilisation rate, i.e. mostly revolving lines that are drawn and used, so loan proceeds are not counted as spare cash; the firm carries the debt and the subsidy cuts its interest bill. DSEDT's approved subsidy (MOP 460m on MOP 3.8bn = 12.1%) equals 4% x 3 years on the full balance.
sources.source: AMCM SME credit, H1 2026; DSEDT reply, Feb 2026

sources.item: Cash buffer profiles: 13 / 27 / 62 days of normal outflows
sources.basis: 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile cash buffer days of 600,000 US small businesses (restaurants' median: 16 days). No comparable distribution is published for Macao or Hong Kong SMEs (a 2020 HKGCC poll only reports that 42% of SMEs expected to last up to six months without relief), so the sensitivity table halves and doubles these buffers.
sources.source: JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Flows, Balances, and Buffer Days (2016)

sources.basis: One standard deviation of each sector's aggregate margin across DSEC survey years 2015-2024, so a weak or strong profile looks like the sector in a bad or good year.

Revenue uncertainty comes only from DSEC sector data (bootstrapped VAR residuals); firm differences come from the margin and cash-buffer profiles. Adding 8% monthly firm noise changed normal-times failure by only 0.3pp, so it was removed rather than assumed.

With no shock and no subsidy, the average profile's 24-month failure rate is 14.4%, against an SME loan delinquency ratio of 8.5% at end-June 2026. Same order of magnitude; the model is somewhat pessimistic because restaurant profiles inherit the sector's negative 2024 margin.

sources.item: Neighbourhood restaurants: 24% visitor demand, rest local (supermarket sales as proxy)
sources.basis: DSEC Tourism Satellite Account: visitors account for 62.2% of restaurant value added (2024). With tourist-facing restaurants at 100%, the neighbourhood type is set so the two average to the industry figure.
DSEC 2024 averages are 5.4 persons per retail and 7.7 per restaurant establishment; 40 represents larger SMEs under the scheme's 100-staff limit.

sources.item: Excess depression after job loss: 9.3 percentage points
sources.basis: East Asian evidence used as the default: in the Korea Welfare Panel (7,368 adults), moving from permanent work to unemployment raised the odds of depression 1.78 times. Applied to the 16% baseline among the employed, that is 25.3% vs 16%. The international meta-analysis (34% vs 16%, i.e. 18 points) is kept as the upper comparator.
sources.source: Yoo et al. (2016), BMJ Open 6(3):e008570; Paul & Moser (2009)

sources.basis: Median duration of a major depressive episode in the general population is 6 months (mean 10.7 months).
sources.source: ten Have et al. (2017), Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica 136(3)

sources.item: Excess mortality +50% in the year after job loss
sources.basis: Two independent sources agree: the lower bound of the 50-100% US estimate, and the international meta-analysis of 42 studies (20 million people), pooled HR 1.63, about 24% lower (roughly 1.48) once health behaviours are controlled. No usable East Asian estimate was found; HR 1.63 is in the sensitivity table.
sources.source: Roelfs et al. (2011), Soc Sci Med 72(6); Sullivan & von Wachter (2009)

sources.basis: Macao's probability of dying between 15 and 60 is 38.8 per 1,000 (UN World Population Prospects 2024), spread evenly over 45 years.

sources.item: 43.5 years of life lost per excess death
sources.basis: DSEC life expectancy at birth 2022-2025 is 83.5 years; minus 40, the displacement age Sullivan & von Wachter use for their life-expectancy illustration.
